_comment: Canonical mutate scope for the SHARED-crypto half of the mutation gate (ADR 0045), split out of web/stryker.mutate.json when this package was extracted (cr-admin-web-extraction, ADR 0065). Read by both packages/crypto/stryker.config.mjs (the mutator) and scripts/mutation_meta_check.py (the guard that asserts something was in fact mutated) — two languages, neither able to parse the other's config, so a restated scope would drift the mutator and its guard apart. Paths are package-relative (Stryker's cwd = packages/crypto/). WHY THE SPLIT IS STRUCTURAL, not a filing preference: Stryker's test runner is the project's own vitest, and a project's vitest does not collect a sibling package's suites — so leaving these two entries in web/'s manifest would have mutated files no web test covers and reported a green run over nothing, the precise failure scripts/mutation_meta_check.py exists to catch. The gate has to live where the tests that kill its mutants live. WHAT IS IN (what the last --force run measured per file is stated once, in stryker.config.mjs's thresholds comment): v1.ts, the KAT-pinned tier every other crypto claim rests on — killed by this package's OWN suite, which is the point: web/'s feature tests also call its exports, but they can never kill a mutant here, and before cr-crypto-mutation-gate-green it scored 83.67 % (--force, 2026-10-01) because nothing in the package called the identity codec, the hybrid halves or the share-password token; and primitives.ts + seal.ts, which are that same tier split out of it (cr-seal-binds-its-object: the raw wraps left the package's exports, and the typed seal that replaced them is the only way a consumer seals) and accountBirth.ts (cr-0177: a seeded-RNG + fixed-identity byte-KAT whose expected wraps use HARDCODED AAD literals, so a mutated source context disagrees; its three Argon KEKs are MOCKED because real Argon is ~2.6 s per buildAccount and Stryker pays that per mutant — KEK byte-correctness is v1.conformance's job). emergencyKit.ts (cr-emergency-kit-codec-in-crypto, inbox #169) is in for the same kind of reason: its value is the parser's VALIDATION branches — version, email type, a Secret Key that decodes to exactly 32 bytes, strict UTF-8 without a BOM — and a round-trip test cannot grade a single one of them, because a round trip only ever feeds the parser what the writer produces. The fixed-literal vector pins the writer; the mutation score is what says each rejection is asserted on its own. WHAT IS OUT, measured not skipped: the argon workers, measured 2026-10-02 by a one-off run with only these two files in `mutate` — argon.worker.ts 100.00% (29 killed: argon.worker.test.ts loads the dispatcher under a stubbed `self` and sends every op) and argonWorker.ts 39.51% (32 killed, 23 survived, 26 NoCoverage: worker-vs-fallback PATH survivors — the tests pin the crypto RESULT, byte-identical either way). Both are execution placement, not crypto; scoring them together reports the misleading number ADR 0045 §3 exists to prevent. base64.ts is out for the same reason it was never in: it is transport encoding with a round-trip test, not crypto logic.
